blurb: Six aboard: a driver, a front passenger and four riders sitting on the back deck's edges, all five shooting their own weapons

notes.model: A Meshy Community sci-fi buggy (Meshy_AI__1108120754, CC0; content/guns.json vehicles/sixer_buggy.glb, 2026-11-11): a tube-frame four-wheeler with a cage over the cabin and an open deck behind it. Its tires are cut out as parts (wheel_*), so they spin, steer and ride the springs. The Tactical Off-Road Beast (on its separate tires) it replaced is the fallback (vehicles/offroad_buggy.glb).
notes.half: Fitted across the tires (2026-11-11, as the Troop Truck's): 2.9 m wide, so walls stop the tires where they are drawn and rounds that hit a tire hit the buggy. Length and height unchanged: the model is 4.4 m long and 1.98 m tall; its body is about 1.8 m wide and its tires stand out to 2.86 m.
notes.seats: Measured on the model (slices of its triangles): two front seats, cushions 0.82 m up at z 0.08 and 0.4 m either side (the floor 0.6 m up, the wheel on the left); behind the cabin's hoop (z -0.6) an open deck 1.7 m up, clear overhead, from x -0.25 to 0.75 (a rack box stands on its left side, x -0.7 to -0.3, 2.0 m) and z -0.6 to -1.45. The four standing riders stand on it two by two (x -0.15 and 0.45, z -0.7 and -1.3: as near the buggy's middle as the rack lets the left pair's feet go, 0.1 m nearer than at first), like the Gun Jeep's standing gunner. The owner's layout, 2026-11-11: a driver, a seated front passenger and four standing in the back. Owner, 2026-11-11 ("if what I asked for doesn't look normal, normalize"): four standing on the small deck looked top-heavy, so the four ride sitting on its edges facing out, like the Gun Jeep's rail riders: the right pair on the deck's edge (1.7 m), the left pair on the rack box (2.0 m), legs over the side.
notes.cockpitEye: A seated head height (1.5 m), under the cage's front bar (1.6 m at z 0.4), looking over the wheel and dash. Up close the driver sees an in-house cockpit instead of the body's own (client content/cockpits.ts), refitted to this body.
notes.vehicle: The Warthog feel: soft, long-travel springs (bouncy, leans out of turns), loose at speed so it powerslides. The suspension's contact points and hub height are the old drawn tires' (unchanged handling).
